page_title: Optics: create it your way, run it forever

sources.entry: Optics Framework - Open-source UI test automation for Android, iOS, web and smart TV apps, with tests written as CSV or YAML steps. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/mozarkai/optics-framework) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Optics Framework
summary.one_liner: Optics is an open-source UI test automation framework for Android, iOS, web and TV apps, where tests are written as CSV or YAML files or recorded, described to an AI agent, or generated via MCP.
use_cases: automate regression tests for Android and iOS apps
write UI tests as spreadsheet CSV steps
record a manual flow on a device and save it as a reusable test
run web and mobile tests in CI on every push
let an AI agent write test suites through MCP
monitor a live app with scheduled test runs
summary.what_it_does: Optics runs test suites step by step against Android, iOS, web, Android TV, Samsung Tizen and LG webOS targets, using Appium for mobile and TV and Selenium or Playwright for web. Tests are split into test cases, modules and elements stored as CSV or YAML files that can be reviewed in pull requests. Each element can be located by XPath, visible text, OCR, or a reference image, with an optional AI self-heal fallback. Runs produce a JUnit XML report, screenshots annotated with what was found, and failures from on-screen error messages. The optics dry_run command validates references without a device.
notable: Four ways to author tests: hand-written CSV/YAML, recording on device, describing flows to an AI agent, or delegating to an agent via optics mcp
Element locators tried in order: XPath, text, OCR, image, then optional AI self-heal
Error definitions in CSV flag crash dialogs or 'Session expired' screens as failures even without an assertion
Also usable as a Python library and Robot Framework library
caveats: AI self-heal and AI describe features need a model such as Gemini, Claude, OpenAI or a local model; the page does not state their cost
Page does not state pricing beyond Apache 2.0 licensing
